title: Time each step of the import duplicate check on one fixed library and one fixed set of files
body: Import a fixed set of files into a fixed copy of a library through the staged import (the path a big zip or folder import takes, `pixlstash/tasks/picture_import_task.py`) and time each step per file: the sampled hash (`pixel_sha`, a SHA-256 of a few small chunks of the file), the full-file SHA-256, the database lookup on the writer thread, the confirmation that re-reads the matching library file, and the creation of the picture with its thumbnail. Run it twice, once with a set that is all new files and once with a set that is all duplicates of pictures already in the library, so the cost of each outcome is seen separately. This does not speed anything up by itself; it says which step is worth attacking, since today the guesses come only from reading the code. It has worked if it gives a per-step table in seconds per file for both sets, repeatable within about 10 percent across two runs, and a per-file total that matches the import's overall wall-clock time.
